RATIONALE

       Secondary education is the sculpting period for youngsters that eventually leads to a
better country. Therefore, it’s pertinent to realise the importance of secondary education
and pick the best curricula for the secondary stages.

        Secondary education is a crucial stage in a student's life, as it serves as a bridge
between middle stage and higher stage of learning or vocational training. It plays a vital
role in developing a student's academic, personal, and social skills, ultimately preparing
them for future success.

         The study at the Secondary stage in classes 11&12 are compartmentalized
 through the studying of selected specialised subjects as required for higher studies in a
 specific direction. The compartmentalized studies couldn’t provide much exposure to
 some vital disciplines/areas of study that are not covered in their specialized field. To
 overcome these issues, ASSEB, Div –II has decided to offer General Studies as a
 compulsory audit subject for the students of all streams. The subject will be assessed
 internally and Grade will be awarded which will be reflected in the marks-sheet. The
 students must have to study the subject and appear in the internal examination
 otherwise their result in the final examination will be declared as INCOMPLETE.

         The aim of introducing General Studies in Class XII is to broaden students'
 perspectives, develop critical thinking, and foster social and cultural awareness and develop a
 holistic understanding of various subjects beyond their chosen specializations delivering
 through a multidisciplinary approach. It will develop communication skills, promote civic
 responsibility, encouraging independent learning, personal and social development and
 penetrates seeds for life-long learning. By covering a range of subjects and skills, General
 Studies aims to give students a broad base of knowledge and the ability to apply it in real-
 world day to day situations. Further, it will stimulate constructive thinking about possible
 forms in advanced courses. The designed course curricula will encourage students to become
 responsible citizens by raising awareness about social issues, promoting scientific temper,
 and appreciating cultural heritage.

  The study of Environmental and General Studies will also motivate and orient them towards
 appearing in competitive examinations. It definitely widens up the horizons and develops the
 personal interests in students with a focus on Cultural, Social and Scientific domains. In
 essence, it is expected that the studying of General Studies in secondary stage is a valuable
 investment in a student's overall development, which will orient towards academic success,
 future careers, and a fulfilling life.
  Importance of studying the subject “General Studies”
 General Studies


1. Developing a Holistic Understanding:
             General Studies) exposes students to a wide range of subjects, including social
sciences, humanities, Mathematics and computational thinking, and current affairs, which helps
them observe the interconnectedness of different fields of knowledge.
             It encourages students to go beyond their specialized subjects and develop a
broader perspective on various aspects of life, society, and the world.
2. Enhancing Critical Thinking and Problem-Solving:

              By analyzing different perspectives and engaging with complex issues, students
develop critical thinking skills, which are essential for making informed decisions and solving
problems effectively.
               The subject encourages students to question, analyze, and evaluate information,
fostering intellectual curiosity and a deeper understanding of the world around them.
3. Preparing for Higher Education and Careers:
              Many competitive exams and higher education courses require a strong
foundation in general knowledge and analytical skills.
              General Studies equips students with the knowledge and skills necessary to
succeed in various academic disciplines and professional fields.
             It also helps students develop communication skills, both verbal and written,
which are crucial for effective communication in academic and professional settings.
4. Fostering Personal Growth:
             General Studies encourages students to understand themselves better, develop
empathy for others, and build positive relationships.
              It also promotes self-directed learning and a lifelong love for learning by
providing a strong foundation of knowledge and skills.


                    LEARNING OBJECTIVES
The Learning objectives of teaching General Studies are as follows:
       o       General Studies promotes self-directed learning and encourages students to
take an active role in their own education.
      •       General Studies teaches students about their rights and responsibilities as
citizens and encourages them to participate in their communities.
      •         The subject provides students with opportunities to apply their knowledge to
real- world situations and to develop their problem-solving skills.
 General Studies

     •       It helps students develop pride in the rich cultural heritage as well as in the
multipronged achievements of the country in various fields such as politics, agriculture,
Science and technology, education and industry.
       o       General Studies helps students develop their verbal and written communication
skills, enabling them to effectively express their ideas and opinions, be conversant with
contemporary socio-economic problems of the country like illiteracy, poverty, social
disharmony, sex or caste discrimination etc.
     •       General Studies aims to teach students how to analyze, evaluate, and interpret
information in a systematic manner.


         In the revised academic course curricula of ASSEB, the subject General Studies is
compulsory for the students of class XII from the academic session 2026-2027. The students
will be assessed through written examination and project work. However, a total mark 50 is
allotted for the subject but the mark secured will not be calculated in the overall result. Instead
of it, grade is awarded based on the marks obtained by the student. The grading scheme for the
subject is as follows...
       Grade                   Percentage             Marking Range
        A                      80%-100%                       40 – 50
        B                      60%-79%                        30 – 39
        C                      40%-59%                        20 – 29
        D                      0%-39%                         0 – 19

                                                   PROJECTS
         A.     Selection of Topic and Student’s observation
    1.          The students may do simple projects, as they like on the themes of the syllabus, where they
                will identify a problem, frame a hypothesis, gather data and analyze it to test the hypothesis.
    2.          As project is carried for completion over a period, it provides a significant opportunity to
                assess both Scholastic and Co scholastic skills of students.
    3.          Project based learning offers a good experience to the students beyond their textbooks and
                classroom lectures..
    4.          The students develop critical thinking skills and the competencies to solve problems
    5.          The students may be assessed on criteria based on few observations. Each may be assigned
                a score out of 04.

    Sl No.     Descriptors                                                                    Score Out
                                                                                              of 04
    01          Demonstrates understanding of the concept of the Project
    02          Has done enough research and collected relevant information
    03          Demonstrates originality in the approach to the project
    04          Resources used like internet, library and other material for the
                completion of the project
    05          Has interpreted the results properly by drawing logical conclusions

    B.          Preparation of Questionnaire and presentation of the project:

             A questionnaire is a list of questions that are answered by many people . It is used to collect
    information about a particular subject. It can be used to collect quantitative and/or qualitative
    information. Generally, it is used as a tool to conduct survey.

    For example – To conduct a survey on the awareness on Financial Literacy of the Common People

    The main Objectives of this survey

   Students will be able to interact with people to find out how alert they are in handling financial
    matters.
   Students will find out how the people become victim of fraudulent groups.
       General Studies

   Students after analyzing the data collected by them will be able to spread the message to the people
    on the importance of Financial Literacy.
   Students will be able to arrange for lectures to the public to share the findings of their survey and
    how alert they should be on financial matters.

    The teacher may facilitate by giving following instructions to the students

   Students may work in groups of five or six on each project. Questionnaire to be used in their locality
    covering age group 17+.
   Each group will prepare a questionnaire having a list of relevant questions or items to be used to
    gather data from respondents. May have a list of open ended questions
   Each group will analyse the data collected by them and will share their findings with others
   After analysing the data collected, feedback to be given to the financial agencies for further action.
    This can be executed in a public forum to create awareness.

    In this stage the students may be assessed on criteria based on few observations. Each may be
    assigned a score out of 06.

    Guidelines:

              1.      Choose any One topics for the Project Work, one each from Units I-X, as
              mentioned in the syllabus.
              2.      The maximum length of the project work is 1000 words.
              3.      The Project Work should be hand-written in A4 sheets, and neatly filed /
              spiral bound. No typed or downloaded material will be accepted.
              4.      The Cover Page to be personalized based on the topics of your choice; along
              with the Name, Roll No., Class & Section.
              5.      The Project Work on each topic should comprise of a maximum of 3 A4
              sheets.
              6.      Pictures/Data should be pasted on the left page along with relevant captions.
              7.      Acknowledgements of the web links, sources, e-journals, magazines, citations
              media reports etc. should be included.
              8.      References from any verbal, visual or written sources must be duly
              acknowledged as a part of the Academic Honesty Policy.
              9.      Case Studies to be included, if found relevant to your topic.
